title: Lakhpat Rai promised to condone the robbing of Sikhs,

blocks.text: Lakhpat Rai promised to condone the robbing of Sikhs only after all of them had been slaughtered, fearing that premature looting would let survivors slip away into the wild. Once that order was given, the Mughals renewed their assault with cannon, cavalry, and close pressure on the trapped Khalsa.

The Singhs answered with a fierce counterattack that briefly drove back mounted assailants and revived their spirits in the middle of disaster. In that moment Sukha Singh resolved that the struggle had to be carried directly against the man directing the slaughter.

Before striking, however, he learned that Lakhpat Rai stood behind a heavy security cordon around him, protected by infantry, horsemen, camel swivels, and artillery. Sukha Singh still tried to reach him, but a small cannon shot smashed one of his legs and broke the attack before it could be completed.
